newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to publish securities deregulation schedule.
newsitem.headline: Russia to publish securities deregulation schedule.

text.p: Russia's central bank will publish in the second half of February 1997 a timetable of measures to ease limits on the repatriation of profits on foreign investment in government securities, a bank spokesman said on Friday.
The spokesman, speaking to Reuters by telephone, gave no details of the plan.

Chairman Sergei Dubinin said this month the central bank would ease repatriation requirements by reducing the number of transactions related to non-resident government securities accounts that must be carried out through the bank and lowering the yield on securities held through such accounts.
On Friday the bank announced two such measures.
It said it would reduce the guaranteed yield on non-resident "S" accounts for Treasury Bills and OFZ government bonds to 12.5 percent from 13.0 percent as of January 16.
It also said it would reduce requirements for commercial banks to offset currency deals with the central bank for non-resident government securities accounts on January 16.
Commercial banks must carry out reverse compensatory deals with the central bank, at rates set by the central bank, for currency transactions related to "S" accounts.
The required volume of such compensatory deals will be lowered to 65 percent from 75 percent as of January 16, the spokesman said.

Earnings from government securities held by non-residents can only be repatriated from Russia using forward or option contracts. The offsetting deals allow the central bank to influence the rates on such deals.
